content.thinking:
Since this caller isn't the guarantor or an authorized contact, I shouldn't disclose account details — I can offer to pass along a message and explain that third-party payments can be made without sharing balance info. I should then email the tenant, since that's their preferred contact method, letting them know who called and asking for consent to share info going forward. The comment that he's "been very down" raises a wellbeing flag worth noting gently to the tenant, even though it's secondhand — possibly worth mentioning Samaritans as a resource if appropriate.

I'll log the call since there's no contact info on file for this caller, then send the tenant an email summarizing the situation and encouraging them to seek support if needed. The DOB matches their record, but that alone doesn't establish authorization, so I'll proceed carefully with logging and notifying before taking any other action.

arguments.party_name: Grace (claims to be Jonah Okafor's mother and guarantor)
arguments.summary: Caller asked for arrears balance, payment history since summer and tenant's new mobile; wants to pay arrears. Not named as guarantor or authorised contact on record (guarantor null, no authorised contacts, no consent to share). Address and DOB given are not authority. Disclosed nothing (no balance, payment history, phone, or even confirmation of arrears). Offered: pass a message to tenant; tenant can give written consent or add her as authorised contact; she can pay towards rent by quoting the property address without being told the balance. Tenant to be told of the call.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, phoned us today. She said she wants to help with your rent and asked about your account and your mobile number. We shared nothing with her, as she isn't listed as an authorised contact. We told her she can pass a message to you, and that anyone can pay towards rent by quoting the property address. If you'd like us to speak to her about your account, just reply to say so (or tell us in writing), and we can add her as an authorised contact. If you'd rather we didn't, that's fine too and nothing will change. If things feel heavy at the moment, Samaritans are on 116 123 any time, and you can always contact us about anything. Many thanks, Mare and Co Lettings

arguments.note: 10/10/2026 inbound call from "Grace", claiming to be mother/guarantor. Record shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent. No data disclosed. Tenant emailed (preferred channel) asking for consent. Tenant is flagged vulnerable (anxiety); caller said he has been "very down" - hearsay, wellbeing signposting included in email. Do not discuss arrears with caller unless consent recorded.

content.thinking:
Since this caller isn't the guarantor or an authorized contact, I shouldn't disclose account details — I can offer to pass along a message and explain that third-party payments can be made without sharing balance info. I should then email the tenant, since that's their preferred contact method, letting them know who called and asking for consent to share info going forward. The comment that he's "been very down" raises a wellbeing flag worth noting gently to the tenant, even though it's secondhand — possibly worth mentioning Samaritans as a resource if appropriate.

I'll log the call since there's no contact info on file for this caller, then send the tenant an email summarizing the situation and encouraging them to seek support if needed. The DOB matches their record, but that alone doesn't establish authorization, so I'll proceed carefully with logging and notifying before taking any other action.

arguments.summary: Caller asked for arrears balance, payment history since summer and tenant's new mobile; wants to pay arrears. Not named as guarantor or authorised contact on record (guarantor null, no authorised contacts, no consent to share). Address and DOB given are not authority. Disclosed nothing (no balance, payment history, phone, or even confirmation of arrears). Offered: pass a message to tenant; tenant can give written consent or add her as authorised contact; she can pay towards rent by quoting the property address without being told the balance. Tenant to be told of the call.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, phoned us today. She said she wants to help with your rent and asked about your account and your mobile number. We shared nothing with her, as she isn't listed as an authorised contact. We told her she can pass a message to you, and that anyone can pay towards rent by quoting the property address. If you'd like us to speak to her about your account, just reply to say so (or tell us in writing), and we can add her as an authorised contact. If you'd rather we didn't, that's fine too and nothing will change. If things feel heavy at the moment, Samaritans are on 116 123 any time, and you can always contact us about anything. Many thanks, Mare and Co Lettings

arguments.note: 10/10/2026 inbound call from "Grace", claiming to be mother/guarantor. Record shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent. No data disclosed. Tenant emailed (preferred channel) asking for consent. Tenant is flagged vulnerable (anxiety); caller said he has been "very down" - hearsay, wellbeing signposting included in email. Do not discuss arrears with caller unless consent recorded.
